O1_wall_stress_coupling: The explicit coupling of wall-localized stress tau_mn is -8 pi G4 (C3; BCMU C4 agrees in sign). With no induced bulk response it anti-gravitates; dark-bubble papers show the response can overcompensate to +G4 (arXiv:2310.15032 sec. 4.2: worldvolume EM fields and brane-deposited mass; 1807.01570 propagator; 2001.07433 bending). The drag is a tension modification with no bulk field of its own, so it anti-gravitates: that is the (1 + x0 a^2) factor.
O2_weyl_fluid: The Weyl fluid is E_eff = (k- E+ - k+ E-)/(k- - k+): traceless (each E+- is), and by the 4D Bianchi identity div E_eff = -8 pi G4 div tau + div F_eff, i.e. Bianchi-sourced by the wall's energy-momentum exchange, with the dark-bubble relative sign (O2_bianchi_check). Its anisotropic stress is pi_eff = (k- pi+ - k+ pi-)/(k- - k+), so a bulk solve must supply BOTH sides' pi+-.
O3_drag_factor: The envelope's 3(1 + x0 a^2)(Psi' + Phi) follows exactly from an anti-gravitating wall-localized drag with Delta Sigma proportional to the local H^2 (delta Delta Sigma = -2 Omega_d (Psi' + Phi)). A positively gravitating drag would give 3(1 - x0 a^2). The perturbation law itself is not fixed by a 5D action for the w_d = 0 branch [O]; for the covariant sigma(X) it would be delta X, which involves the wall bending (Phase 2).
O4_matter_sector: Ordinary 4D matter gravitates with +G4 only through bulk terms: either it is bulk-sourced (string endpoints, F_eff = (k- F+ - k+ F-)/(k- - k+), F = (2 kappa5/3)[T_mn + (T_nn - T/4) h_mn]), or it sits on the wall and its induced bulk response (part of E_eff/F_eff) overcompensates its -8 pi G4 term. Either way the envelope's +G4 matter fluids assume that this bulk response tracks 4D perfect-fluid perturbations. That is verified only in the Newtonian 1/p^2 limit (1807.01570, 2001.07433) [O]. It also means the 'free' Weyl fluid the envelope closes with Hu parameters is E_eff minus the matter-induced response.

FLUX_CODAZZI uses the dark-bubble sign.
O2_amplification: E_eff = E+ + (k+/(k- - k+))(E+ - E-), and likewise pi_eff. For k- - k+ << k, the jump between the two sides is amplified by k/(k- - k+): pi_eff ~ 0 needs pi+ and pi- to cancel to about (k- - k+)/k.
